summary.text: Royal Cinque Ports, known as Deal, is a tough Kent links that hosted the Open in 1909 and 1920.

setting.text: The course runs along the coast of Sandwich Bay at Deal, on the same stretch of coastline as Royal St George's and Prince's.
Top100golfcourses calls it 'an absolute brute of a links', with the last seven holes invariably playing into the prevailing south-westerly wind.
Top100golfcourses describes the layout as stark and out-and-back, defined only by sandhills and wild dune grasses, with tight and hanging lies.
Peter Alliss said of Deal: 'Straight out and straight back, the inward nine, especially if there is a wind against, is perhaps as formidable as anything in British golf.'

history.text: The club was founded in 1892. Its name comes from Deal's membership of the Cinque Ports, an ancient group of trading towns given special privileges by medieval monarchs.
Henry Hunter, the first greenkeeper, was appointed soon after founding. Three months later a nine-hole course was ready, and a second nine was soon added.
The two World Wars did much damage to the links. James Braid restored it for reopening in 1919, and Sir Guy Campbell did the same, reopening it in 1946.
It was the third English course, after Royal St George's and Royal Liverpool, to host the Open.
J. H. Taylor won the first Open at Deal in 1909, on 295.
George Duncan won the 1920 Open here. Abe Mitchell led by six after the first day and Duncan was 13 back, but Duncan shot 71 and 72 on the last day while Mitchell had 84 and 76.
Walter Hagen boasted before the 1920 Open that he was unbeatable, and finished 55th.
Abe Mitchell was a member of the Cantelupe Club, the artisan section at Royal Ashdown Forest, according to Top100golfcourses.
Open Championships were scheduled for Deal in 1938 and 1949, but abnormally high tides flooded the course and both were played at Royal St George's. The club left the Open rota.
The club has hosted the Amateur Championship in 1923, 1982 and 2013, and has hosted the Public Schools Championship every year since 1925.
It remains a final qualifying course for the Open, most recently in 2025.
Martin Ebert has advised on continuing course improvements, according to Top100golfcourses.

trivia.text: Gary Player said: 'I consider the last four holes at Deal to be without doubt, the finest four consecutive holes on any course in the world.'
James Braid wrote that Deal was 'the best course in England', quoted by the club.
Bernard Darwin wrote: 'Golf at Deal is very good indeed - fine, straight-ahead, long hitting golf wherein the fives are likely to be many and the fours few.'
Only Royal Portrush and Prince's have hosted fewer Opens, according to Top100golfcourses.
The black tees play to 7,367 yards, with par 72 on the club scorecard quoted by Wikipedia.
Top100golfcourses' 2015 Kent county ranking put Royal Cinque Ports 2nd in Kent, behind Royal St George's.

3.text: The par 5 3rd was lengthened in 2019, with the tee moved to the left of the 2nd green. It heads towards a punchbowl green.

16.text: The 16th is now a par 5 with a split fairway. Top100golfcourses says it gives some respite when heading home into the wind.

local.text: Deal is a town on the Kent coast. Royal Cinque Ports sits on Golf Road in Deal.
Royal St George's and Prince's lie close by on the same stretch of coastline.
